source.title: TRACE for Tracking the Emergence of Semantic Representations in Transformers
source.authors: N. Aljaafari; Danilo S. Carvalho; André Freitas

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the grokking literature to motivate extended training, but its own results do not test the delayed train/test-accuracy behaviour or the specific mechanisms in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study trains small transformers on synthetic English-like sentences and reports representational and output-performance dynamics. It does not report training accuracy saturating while test accuracy stays at chance and later rises, a training-set-size sweep, or experiments on the mechanisms named in the versions. Its terminal performance table is not a training-versus-test accuracy trajectory. Rows below capture related measured dynamics, not direct tests of a claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper cites grokking to justify extended training (500 epochs) and says this was meant to check whether grokking occurs. It reports no train-versus-held-out accuracy trajectory, no delayed rise after overfitting, and no dataset-size, weight-norm or optimizer manipulation. Its results are curvature, intrinsic-dimension and probe dynamics on synthetic English-like text. Output accuracy is said to improve and stabilise early, but the split is not stated. These measure related constructs, not any version's behaviour.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. Additions: the authors frame the transitions as a shift from memorisation to abstraction. They say this shift appears as phase transitions rather than gradual change, and is robust across model scales and FFN or attention-head ablations. They also say mutual information was too noisy to serve as a diagnostic, and that their results are correlational.
record.recipe_differences: Uses next-token training on a synthetic frame-semantic language corpus and tracks curvature, intrinsic dimension, probes, and generation performance; it does not reproduce the original algorithmic grokking setup or measure its train/test accuracy pattern.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that transition timing and stability vary with model scale and architectural changes; smaller models transition later, and removing feed-forward blocks or reducing attention heads affects volatility and timing.

fits_no_version.finding: Small transformers on synthetic frame-semantic text show a curvature-collapse / intrinsic-dimension-stabilisation intersection. It comes earlier in larger models (about step 5000) than in smaller ones (after step 30000). Output accuracy stabilises early while internal probe confidence keeps reorganising.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal representational phase transitions in language-like training can lag output accuracy and scale in timing with model capacity.

record.problems: The data are synthetic and do not capture the full richness of natural language. The paper says its correlations do not establish causal relationships. For the claim at issue, it provides no train/test accuracy trajectory, and does not report uncertainty estimates for the averaged results.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; four related results are retained. Terminal generation metrics in Table 3 are not included because they do not report a delayed-generalization trajectory.

untested.parts: No algorithmic dataset, no train/test accuracy gap over time, no training-set-size sweep.
No circuit identification, no memorization-component removal, no progress measure tested against a test-accuracy jump.
Uses non-algorithmic (synthetic language) data, but reports no delayed held-out generalization and no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
Tiny models (110K to 749K params) on synthetic data; no realistic LLM training.
No weight decay variation, critical dataset size or ungrokking; 'minimal regularisation' is used throughout.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
Adam only; no optimizer or numerical controls.

missing.what: Authors say training was extended to check whether grokking occurs, but report no outcome (no train-versus-held-out curve). A researcher would need to know that no grokking result is given.

record.verdict_notes: T4 is borderline with T6: grokking serves only as motivation for training length. There are no held-out accuracy dynamics, so no version gets a verdict. Table 3 gives only terminal metrics after the phase transition.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic dataset, train/test accuracy trajectory, delayed rise after overfitting, or training-set-size comparison.
No generalizing circuit identification, Fourier algorithm, memorizing-component removal, or test-accuracy jump anticipated by progress measures.
No test of grokking-like delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data or switch involving initialization scale or weight norm.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
No comparison of weight decay or other low-norm bias, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
No controls for adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point softmax limits.

rows.subject: Small model
rows.operation_detail: Tracked Hessian curvature and intrinsic dimension during training.
rows.measure: Curvature-ID intersection as an indicator of representational phase transition
rows.value: Delayed transition (after step 30000); lower equilibrium ID values than larger models.
rows.note: The paper describes an abstraction-related representational transition, not delayed test-accuracy generalization.
rows.check: Curvature-ID intersection is a geometric marker, not delayed test-accuracy generalization; the link to none is correct.

rows.subject: Medium model
rows.operation_detail: Tracked Hessian curvature and intrinsic dimension during training.
rows.measure: Curvature-ID intersection as an indicator of representational phase transition
rows.value: Qualitatively similar transition, with persistent periodic curvature spikes.
rows.note: The transition timing is not quantified in the text; this is not a train/test accuracy result.
rows.check: Same construct as r1; no timing value is given, so the value is qualitative only.

rows.subject: Large model
rows.operation_detail: Tracked Hessian curvature and intrinsic dimension during training.
rows.measure: Curvature-ID intersection as an indicator of representational phase transition
rows.value: Intersection occurs early (around step 5000) and sharply.
rows.note: The paper describes curvature collapse and ID plateau, not a delayed test-accuracy rise.
rows.check: Same construct as r1; the step-5000 timing is read from text, and the figure is not quantified.

rows.subject: Models across scales (aggregate; small, medium, and large)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked semantic output-classification accuracy during training.
rows.value: Accuracy rapidly improves and stabilises early in training.
rows.note: The text does not specify a training-versus-test accuracy comparison or give a numerical trajectory. The authors contrast early output accuracy with continuing internal representational change.
rows.check: Output semantic accuracy (Fig. 4) is reported without saying whether it is train or held-out data, and with no training-accuracy comparison, so it cannot show or rule out a grokking delay. The text's 'rapidly improves and stabilises early' suggests no delayed jump, but the split is unclear.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
